record.source_text: For assets that already formed part of the business assets at the end of the preceding fiscal year, the taxpayer may in the following fiscal years recognize the partial value even if that value is higher than the last book value; however, at most the acquisition or production costs may be recognized. b) In the case of agricultural and forestry businesses, the valuation of assets subject to biological growth may be made at the partial value exceeding acquisition or production costs. c) In the statement of assets and liabilities (annual financial statement, balance sheet), a write-down of up to 15% of the amount of the receivable outstanding at the respective balance sheet date may be taken on foreign receivables if the following conditions are met: — The receivables were acquired from supplies pursuant to Section 6 nos. 1 to 3 of the Turnover Tax Act 1972 or from services performed abroad for foreign customers (Section 7(1) no. 1 of the Turnover Tax Act 1972). — The flat-rate write-down is reported for the first time in the balance sheet of the fiscal year in which the receivables arose. — The flat-rate write-down is reversed on a profit-increasing basis as the receivables are collected.
